summary: Turns an operator's parameter dialog into an interactive panel, with controls for including headers, pages, labels, built-in/custom parameters, scoped page/parameter patterns, compression, and expansion permissions.

key_params.name: header
key_params.note: Show OP type, name, and header controls

key_params.name: separators
key_params.note: Show separator lines between parameter sections

key_params.name: inputeditor
key_params.note: Include multi-input editor UI when available

key_params.name: allowexpand
key_params.note: Allow users to expand parameters to see modes and expression editing

key_params.name: combinescopes
key_params.note: Combine page and parameter scopes with Any or All behavior

key_params.name: pagescope
key_params.note: Page-name pattern selection, including quoted names with spaces

key_params.name: syncpage
key_params.note: Sync selected displayed page with the target parameter dialog

key_params.name: scopeorder
key_params.note: Order parameters by Parameter Scope when page names are hidden

key_concepts: Parameter COMP turns another operator's parameter dialog into an interactive panel interface.
It can include the target header, page tabs, labels, separators, input editor, built-in parameters, and custom parameters.
Page Scope and Parameter Scope use pattern matching to expose a curated subset of controls.
Allow Expansion controls whether users can open parameter mode and expression editing fields from the panel.
Scope ordering and page synchronization determine whether the panel behaves like a focused control surface or a full parameter dialog.
common_gotchas: Parameter Scope order matters when displaying parameters only; the UI follows the specified order.
Page and parameter scopes use pattern matching, so broad patterns such as * can expose more UI than intended.
Page names with spaces must be quoted or provided as a Python list.
Allow Expansion controls whether users can open parameter mode and expression editing fields.
Compressing the UI can make parameter panels fit smaller spaces but may reduce readability or edit affordance.
Built-In and Custom toggles are independent; include both when exposing a full operator parameter interface.
